title: Priority-driven column collapse, chart-canvas fallbacks, and modal interaction polish for Console dashboards & cost views
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype responsive behaviors and cross-browser fallbacks for the Console dashboard, rollouts, and cost pages. Focus areas: dynamic column prioritization for wide tables, graceful downgrade of chart rendering when canvas features are limited, and modal stacking/interactions that break on some browsers and mobile. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototypes, a front-end implementation checklist for engineering, accessibility notes, and a short cross-browser QA matrix.
background: Recent QA and customer reports surfaced inconsistent rendering and interaction issues across combinations of browsers and devices: charts flicker or do not render when GPU acceleration or OffscreenCanvas is unavailable; dense cost tables overflow horizontally on narrow windows; modals lose scroll lock on iOS Safari when multiple overlays stack. These issues affect console dashboards, rollout detail pages, and cost breakdown tables used by customers to understand spend and traffic patterns.
acceptance_criteria: On viewports < 960px: tables prioritize columns based on priority attribute and collapse lower-priority columns into a single expandable summary column
Charts default to Canvas rendering, but fall back to vector SVG or precomputed raster tiles when OffscreenCanvas or WebGL contexts fail; fallback should preserve data-to-pixel mapping and tooltips
Modals maintain focus trap, body scroll lock, and correct stacking order across Chrome, Safari (iOS/macOS), and Firefox; nested modal pattern replaced with lightweight sheet pattern on small screens
Cost breakdown cards reflow into single-column expandable sections on mobile, preserving the ordering and aria-labels for screen readers
Design tokens and spacing adjustments documented and shipped in component library tokens v2.14
review_feedback: PM: prefer progressive enhancement over feature-detection-heavy logic; provide clear fallback UX for chart failures
Engineering: request explicit guidance on priority rules for columns and a decision matrix for when to swap canvas -> svg -> raster
Accessibility reviewer: ensure collapsed column content remains accessible via keyboard and screen reader; provide aria-expanded on the summary column
decisions_made: Use a 'priority' meta attribute on table columns (0..3) to drive responsive collapse order

Chart rendering order: Canvas -> SVG vector -> rasterized PNG tile. Render engine will try to initialize OffscreenCanvas first and fall back if initialization throws or frame rates are below threshold
Replace nested modal pattern with 'modal + bottom-sheet' hybrid on < 720px to avoid stacking focus issues on mobile Safari
Introduce a small 'render-health' telemetry ping from client to indicate frequent chart fallback occurrences for ops to monitor
tasks: Design: produce Figma variants for desktop/tablet/mobile and annotate collapse rules (Maya)
Engineering: implement column-priority API on Table component and expose collapse breakpoint hooks (ENG-3301)
Engineering: add chart renderer with fallback layers and feature detection (ENG-3368)
QA: build cross-browser visual regression tests for charts and modals on macOS Safari, iOS Safari, Chrome, Firefox
Product: coordinate canary rollout on console-2026.03 and draft customer notification if behavior changes visible
browser_quirks_and_notes: iOS Safari: body scroll locking via position:fixed causes content jump; use -webkit-overflow-scrolling fallback and focus management
Firefox: custom scrollbar width affects layout measurements for dense tables; account for scrollbar-inset in collapse thresholds
Edge (Chromium): GPU-based canvas sometimes forces high CPU; include an init timeout to fall back to SVG
Older Chromium variants may not support OffscreenCanvas; detect via try/catch on OffscreenCanvas constructor
accessibility_notes: Collapsed columns must be reachable via keyboard. Summary collapsed item should expose aria-controls to the hidden column contents and aria-expanded state. When switching chart renderers, ensure tooltip content is still accessible and announce data-load fallback to screen reader users via live-region when rendering fails.
test_plan: Create a visual QA checklist and automated Cypress scenarios: 1) Resize desktop to mobile and verify column collapse order; 2) Simulate OffscreenCanvas failure by mocking and assert fallback to SVG with identical tooltips; 3) Modal stacking: open modal, open nested sheet, verify focus trap and no body scroll on iOS Safari; 4) Accessibility: run axe-core on variants and fix critical violations.
rollout_strategy: Canary on 5% of traffic for console-2026.03, monitor 'render-health' telemetry and console errors for 72 hours. If fallback rates exceed 1% of chart renders in canary, auto-roll back and capture bug dash. Gradually increase to 50% over a week with QA sign-off.

Schedule cross-team review on 2026-03-04 to align on telemetry and canary thresholds
